# OSSDrop

> OSSDrop is a curated, community-maintained list of open-source tools,
> organized by category. Makers add their own tool with one pull request.
> Every entry has a public repository and an OSI-approved license. Listing
> is free; rankings cannot be bought.

## Key facts

- Tagline: "Drop your open-source tool."
- Categories: AI & Coding Agents, Developer Tools & CLI, Data & Databases,
  DevOps & Self-Hosted, Productivity, Security & Privacy, Web & APIs,
  Creator / Media.
- Tables are sorted by live GitHub star count; "Trending this week" is
  computed from daily star snapshots, not editorial choice.
- List content is public domain (CC0-1.0); each linked tool keeps its own
  license.

## Data

- [tools.json](https://github.com/OSSDrop/list/blob/main/data/tools.json):
  machine-readable source of truth for all listed tools (name, repo,
  homepage, category, description, license).
- [README](https://github.com/OSSDrop/list/blob/main/README.md): the
  human-readable directory, regenerated nightly.
- [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/OSSDrop/list/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
  how to add a tool (one JSON object, one PR).

## Where OSSDrop lives

- GitHub organization: https://github.com/OSSDrop
- Reddit community: https://www.reddit.com/r/OSSDrop/
- Website: https://ossdrop.com (coming soon)
